text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Wednesday with most of the activity in unlinked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 104.65
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 to 103.70
Volume, mostly concentrated in the Makam and unlinked bonds, was a moderate 167 million shekels.
"Despite today's rise the market is very stable and it continues to be very quiet," said one trader.
"CPI-linked bonds rose sharply but it's meaningless. The rise was an outcome of a rise of 3.1 percent in one series which rose sharply on a very low volume," he said.
A trader at the First International Bank of Israel (FIBI) noted that most of the activity was concentrated in unlinked bonds.
"Funds which specialise in unlinked bonds were buying these bonds back after they sold them before the end of the month to gain tax benefits," he said.
"Makams were also rising but on a much slower pace on a relatively high volume of 77 million shekels. The moderate rise did not affect yields which remained unchanged," the FIBI trader said.

Dollar-linked bonds fell sharply following the rise of the shekel against the dollar on Tuesday. In local trading, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3570 shekels, unchanged from Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
